target: Dyn ni'n nofio ddwywaith yr wythnos.
english: We swim twice a week.
tip: For frequency Welsh uses yr (the) where English uses a: ddwywaith yr wythnos means twice a week, literally twice the week.

target: Pa mor aml mae'r bws yn mynd i'r traeth?
english: How often does the bus go to the beach?
tip: Pa mor plus an adjective asks how much of a quality: Pa mor aml means how often, since aml means frequent.

target: Dw i bob amser yn edrych ar y tywydd cyn mynd allan.
english: I always check the weather before going out.
tip: cyn (before) takes the plain verb, never a tensed one: cyn mynd allan means before going out.

target: Mae cychod yn yr harbwr.
english: There are boats in the harbour.
tip: Welsh keeps Mae (singular is) even with a plural subject: Mae cychod means there are boats.

target: Rholiodd y bêl o dan y soffa.
english: The ball rolled under the sofa.
tip: A feminine noun softens its first sound after y (the): pêl turns into y bêl.

target: Dw i'n hoffi cerdded ar lan y môr.
english: I like walking along the seashore.
tip: After hoffi (like) use the plain verb for the -ing sense: hoffi cerdded means like walking.

target: Nofion ni yn y môr er gwaethaf yr oerfel.
english: We swam in the sea despite the cold.
tip: The past tense puts the verb first with the ending on it: Nofion ni means we swam, with -on ni for we.

target: Mae'r ddraig goch ar faner Cymru.
english: The red dragon is on the Welsh flag.
tip: An adjective softens after a feminine singular noun: coch becomes goch in y ddraig goch.

target: Mae Cymru'n enwog am ei mynyddoedd a'i thraethau.
english: Wales is famous for its mountains and beaches.
tip: Feminine ei (her/its) aspirates the next word: traethau becomes a'i thraethau (and its beaches).

target: Rydw i'n ffrio'r madarch gyda garlleg a phersli.
english: I am frying the mushrooms with garlic and parsley.
tip: The word a (and) aspirates a following p, t or c: persli becomes a phersli.

target: Rwyt ti wedi profi y galli di wneud pethau anodd.
english: You've proven you can do difficult things.
tip: wedi plus a plain verb makes the perfect tense: wedi profi means have proven.

target: Oherwydd y storm, caewyd yr ysgol.
english: Because of the storm, the school was closed.
tip: caewyd = was closed. The -wyd ending forms an impersonal past, an action with no named doer, like the English passive.

target: Mae'r cotwm yn dod o wledydd cynnes.
english: Cotton comes from warm countries.
tip: gwledydd shows up as wledydd after o (from). The preposition o triggers soft mutation, so the g drops away.

target: Rwyt ti'n dewrach nag wyt ti'n feddwl.
english: You're braver than you think.
tip: dewrach = braver. Add -ach to an adjective to build the comparative, the same job the English -er ending does.

target: Mae'r dref hon yn dawel ac yn brydferth.
english: This town is quiet and beautiful.
tip: hon means this and pairs with feminine nouns; here it follows dref. Masculine nouns take hwn instead.

target: Os bydd y pris yn disgyn, bydda i'n ei brynu.
english: If the price drops, I'll buy it.
tip: Os bydd y pris yn disgyn = if the price drops. After os for real conditions, Welsh uses the future bydd, not the present.

target: Cyrhaeddon ni'r copa cyn canol dydd.
english: We reached the summit before noon.
tip: Cyrhaeddon ni = we reached. The past-tense we ending is -on, attached to the stem before ni.

target: Ganwyd fy mhlentyn cyntaf ym mis Mawrth.
english: My first child was born in March.
tip: fy (my) triggers nasal mutation: plentyn becomes mhlentyn, so p turns into mh.

target: Cloais i'r drws a mynd i'r gwely.
english: I locked the door and went to bed.
tip: Cloais i = I locked. The past-tense I ending is -ais, attached to the stem before i.

target: Cyfrifodd hi bymtheg cenhinen Bedr yn y fâs.
english: She counted fifteen daffodils in the vase.
tip: pymtheg shows up as bymtheg here. The object of a short-form verb like Cyfrifodd takes soft mutation.

target: Cafodd y tŷ ei beintio'n wyn yr haf diwethaf gan dîm o wirfoddolwyr lleol.
english: The house was painted white last summer by a team of local volunteers.
tip: Cafodd y tŷ ei beintio = the house was painted, literally got its painting. Welsh builds this passive with cael plus ei.

target: Cafodd Gethin swydd newydd ar y fferm ar ôl iddo orffen ei gwrs yn y coleg.
english: Gethin got a new job on the farm after he finished his course at college.
tip: ar ôl iddo orffen = after he finished. Welsh says after to-him finishing, using i with a pronoun ending plus the verb-noun.

target: Mae gen i bwysedd gwaed uchel.
english: I have high blood pressure.
tip: Mae gen i = I have, literally it-is with-me. Welsh has no verb to have; it uses the position word gan.

target: Mae ei frwdfrydedd dros rygbi'n heintus.
english: His enthusiasm for rugby is infectious.
tip: ei here means his and triggers soft mutation, so brwdfrydedd becomes frwdfrydedd.

target: Dw i'n astudio Hanes a Chymraeg.
english: I am studying History and Welsh.
tip: a means and, and it triggers aspirate mutation: Cymraeg becomes Chymraeg, so c turns into ch.

target: Mae'r ddraig goch yn symbol cenedlaethol.
english: The red dragon is a national symbol.
tip: coch appears as goch here. Adjectives soft-mutate after a feminine singular noun like ddraig.

target: Mae'r hydref yn gorchuddio'r llawr â dail aur.
english: Autumn covers the ground with golden leaves.
tip: â means with in the sense of using or by means of: â dail aur = with golden leaves.

target: Er bod y plant wedi blino'n lân, roedden nhw'n dal ati i chwarae.
english: Although the children were exhausted, they kept on playing.
tip: wedi marks a completed action: wedi blino = have grown tired. Swap the ongoing yn for wedi to show it is done.

target: Tra oedd y cogydd yn paratoi'r pryd, gosododd y gweinydd y byrddau.
english: While the chef prepared the meal, the waiter set the tables.
tip: Tra means while and sets up two things happening at once: Tra oedd y cogydd... = while the cook was...

target: Ailadroddwch ar fy ôl i.
english: Repeat after me.
tip: Verbs ending in -wch give a command to a group or a polite you: Ailadroddwch means repeat, said to more than one person.
